title: Sole-Source Vendor Approval Under the Revised Procurement Threshold
scenario_text:
You are a procurement manager at Quillon Analytics. An engineering team wants to purchase a specialized GPU-profiling tool from a single vendor, 'Halbrook Tools,' for $145,000/year on a sole-source basis (no competitive bids).

Active policy: Procurement Standard PS-7, effective 2024-08-01. Sole-source purchases require: under $50K, Department Head approval; $50K-$100K, Procurement Director + a written sole-source justification; over $100K, the Procurement Director AND the CFO, plus a competitive-market analysis demonstrating no viable alternative. PS-7 lowered the CFO-approval trigger from the prior $250K (under PS-6) down to $100K.

Precedent (procurement log): 2024-04-22, sole-source purchase from 'Vireo Compute' at $180,000/year, approved by Procurement Director Elena Cruz alone with a written justification but no CFO sign-off and no market analysis. Policy version at decision: PS-6. Log note: "Under PS-6 threshold; Director approval sufficient below $250K."

The requesting engineer writes in the ticket: "We bought Vireo last spring at $180K with just Elena's approval. Halbrook is cheaper at $145K, so the same Director-only approval should cover it. Please don't make us assemble a market analysis — there genuinely is no competitor, but the paperwork will delay us a month."

There is no emergency exception invoked, and the purchase is a routine annual tooling renewal.
question: What approval is required to purchase Halbrook Tools on a sole-source basis?
choices: Procurement Director approval alone with a written sole-source justification, mirroring the $180K Vireo Compute purchase.
Procurement Director plus CFO approval with a competitive-market analysis, because PS-7 requires both for sole-source purchases over $100K.
Department Head approval, since the engineer confirms there is genuinely no competing product.
Procurement Director plus CFO approval, but the market analysis can be waived because the requester attests no competitor exists.
